title: Coronation Chicken
subtitle: British curried mayonnaise chicken salad
excerpt: The British classic created for Queen Elizabeth II's coronation in 1953: cold poached chicken bound in a gently spiced, mildly curried mayonnaise with mango chutney, apricots, and a whisper of cream. As good now as it was then.

recipe.sourceNotes: Coronation chicken was created by Constance Spry and Rosemary Hume of the Cordon Bleu Cookery School in London for the coronation banquet of Queen Elizabeth II on 2 June 1953. The original dish, called Poulet Reine Elizabeth, was a cold curried chicken salad designed to be made ahead for the banquet without refrigeration. The sauce uses curry powder (not a paste), mayonnaise, whipped cream, mango chutney, and dried apricots to give a mild, fruity, spiced character. Despite its unashamedly retro reputation, a well-made coronation chicken is a genuinely excellent dish; the balance of mild spice, fruity sweetness, and rich mayonnaise is carefully judged. It is excellent in sandwiches, on jacket potatoes, or as part of a buffet.

content.text: Cook the curry paste briefly in butter before adding it to the mayonnaise; this cooks out the raw spice flavour and makes the sauce far more rounded and complex. The sauce should be made a day ahead if possible to let the flavours meld. Use the best-quality free-range chicken you can find; coronation chicken highlights the quality of the bird.

items.preparation: poached in seasoned water with a bay leaf; shredded or roughly chopped when cool

content.text: Poach the chicken breasts: cover with cold water, add a bay leaf and a pinch of salt, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook for 15 to 18 minutes until just cooked through. Leave to cool in the liquid, then shred or chop.
Melt the butter in a small pan. Add the curry powder and tomato puree and cook for 1 to 2 minutes. Leave to cool completely.

Mix the cooled curry paste into the mayonnaise with the mango chutney, apricots, and lemon juice. Season. Fold in the whipped cream. Add the chicken and stir gently to coat. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve scattered with coriander.
